response:
I don't have file access in this session, so this is a review of the document as written — I haven't verified the line cites or the numbers against the repo.

## What's strong

The honesty is genuinely unusual: you quote a third-party verdict *against* yourself in the header, you record a refuted claim ("reinventing badly" NOT supported), and you kill a $25 experiment on power grounds rather than running it for the sunk narrative. #302 and #303 are the best-reasoned items here. The problem in this plan is not candor. It's allocation.

## The central problem: the remedy reproduces the disease

Your own verdict is that 100% of open work went to the measuring apparatus while lever 1 produced nothing, and that the failure mode is "mistaking the cleanup of the lab's conscience for progress on the product." Then:

- **P0** = the lab's front door
- **P1** = the lab's own rule about itself
- **P2** = five instrument decisions
- **P2b** = the lab's name
- **P3** = the only product work, listed last, *and gated behind P1*
- plus a **~10pd substrate swap** endorsed in the status header

That's another lap. The numbering is doing sneaky work: P0–P2 are ordered by cheapness and P3 by value, and every past month that ordering has meant P3 loses. If lever 1 is the goal, it should be P1 in the document, whatever ships first in practice.

Concretely: **decouple iter4 authoring from P1.** The re-measure *bar* depends on P1; writing building-skills iter4 (the char-negative reshape its own ledger already names) does not. Start it now, in parallel. Right now your entire product track is blocked on one owner's merge queue for #321 — say what happens if that doesn't land this week.

## The ADOPT track needs to be a section, not a header line

~10 person-days to swap onto Inspect AI is the largest single commitment in the document and it appears only in the status preamble. Give it its own section that answers one question: **what product decision changes because you have runtime dollar limits, multi-provider judging, and sandboxing?** If the honest answer is "none in the next quarter," defer it — it is apparatus work at the exact moment the diagnosis says stop. Also unaddressed: what happens to comparability with the existing benchmark corpus. Are 18-Jul verdicts still reproducible post-swap, or does the swap silently invalidate the ledger P1 is about to create?

## P0 should be mechanical, not manual

Six of the nine P0 items are stale cross-references, a duplicated constant, and a mis-stated number. You are hand-scrubbing a class of defect that will re-accumulate in the next 18 commits — the same 18 commits that produced P1. You already have `adr-lint`; extend it:

- cite-existence check (kills items 4, 5, and the ADR 0016 gap)
- constant-duplication check, or make `building-skills/SKILL.md` read the limits from `validate.py` (item 8)
- **measured-status freshness**: auto-generate "measured 18-Jul, N unmeasured edits since" next to each verdict from git

That last one is the actual fix for truth-in-labeling, and it's also the enforcement mechanism P1 option (b) needs. Ship P0 as lint rules and the class doesn't come back.

## P1: option (b) is right, but a ledger without a service policy is just a growing to-do list

Specify at decision time: what triggers a batch (edit count? char delta? cadence?), the max debt before it blocks merges, and what a skill's public label says while carrying debt. Also be explicit in the ADR that (b) is a real cost to the pitch — "never on faith" becomes "measured at baseline, with disclosed debt." That's defensible, but it should be stated prominently in the README, not softened into a footnote.

## P2, item by item

**#303 — right call, wrong artifact.** Coverage 0.948–0.970 isn't just "at/above nominal"; above-nominal means the interval is *conservative*, i.e. you're spending power you already don't have at G=6. Say that, since P1's whole argument leans on MDE ~0.35. And close it by shipping a **rule** — a pre-reg field that refuses "strong" language below G=8 — not a note in a session log.

**#317 — weakest item.** You establish that n-grams understate the coupling because the real DV is house doctrine ("frontmatter order", "cut Background"), and then recommend shipping the trigram overlap report as the standing caveat. A caveat that prints 1.4–3.6% will be read as "leakage is small," which inverts your finding. Either report doctrine coupling directly (even a hand-coded checklist of house-isms scored against the rubric) or keep the caveat qualitative and don't attach a reassuring number to it. Bigger gap: you say future doctrine-heavy benchmarks need task-value outcomes, but say nothing about the **existing** verdicts — and the contaminated ones are building-skills and engineering-principles, the two most load-bearing. What is their status as of this plan?

**#302 — good kill, but you buried the best experiment in the repo.** C5 (building-skills vs bare, with a live loss condition, where the competitor's own guide claims the skill shouldn't need to exist) is the only proposed test of lever 1 in the entire document. Promote it out of the #302 bullet to a headline item. Two conditions: state the expected effect size up front — at G=10 MDE 0.17–0.26, running it underpowered yields an INCONCLUSIVE that everyone will read as a KILL — and pair it with its spend decision in the same /decide, or it violates your own P3 stop-list ("no pre-reg drafting without a spend decision").

**#310 — agree with the recommendation**, but note the meta-point: overriding sweep-state's "4 more rounds owed" means the tool's stopping rule is wrong. Fix the rule, or it will make this claim again.

## P2b contradicts your own header

The header says ADR 0097 rename to skill-assay is CONFIRMED by the owner. P2b still reads "Decide: rename plugin vs README disambiguation suffices." A stale internal cross-reference, in the document whose P0 is about stale cross-references. Fix it.

Separately, **"executes LAST" looks like the wrong ordering.** Every P0 and P2 doc edit touches names and paths the rename will churn, so you'll do the labeling scrub twice. The rename is mechanical; run it first, or at minimum don't hand-edit files it will rewrite.

## The missing number

Every figure in this plan is about the instrument: coverage, MDE, containment %, char counts, corpus overlap. There is not one lever-1 number anywhere — no adopters, no external issues, no install count, no adopter interview. That asymmetry is *why* P3 keeps losing: instrument work arrives with numbers attached and product work doesn't. Pick one lever-1 metric and track it in this document with the same seriousness as coverage, or "rebalance toward lever 1" stays unfalsifiable and you'll write this same paragraph next month.

## Minor

The status header has become a changelog and is now the least readable part of the doc — move the decision history to a log and keep the header to current state. ADR numbers are cited without titles in most places. And the /sweep evaluation at the end is a status note, not a plan item; it's also, itself, more lab-conscience work.
